disease_label_per_paper: Lymphoproliferative disease-related mixed cryoglobulinemia treated with rituximab and prednisolone
presentation_summary: 65-year-old Japanese woman with a 3-year relapsing rash history and 3 months of proteinuria was admitted for evaluation.
Examination showed blood pressure 158/84 mmHg, pulse 84/min, temperature 37.0 C, bilateral pitting edema to the thighs, and raised purpuric lesions on both legs.
Urine protein/creatinine ratio was 3.6 g/g Cr, urine protein was 2.7 g/day, sediment had >100 RBC/HPF, 10-19 WBC/HPF, RBC casts, and granular casts.

Laboratory data showed hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, creatinine 1.61 mg/dL, albumin 2.9 g/dL, CRP 4.4 mg/dL, RF 167 IU/mL, C3 45 mg/dL, C4 5.9 mg/dL, CH50 <5 U/mL, and qualitative serum cryoglobulin positivity.
Renal biopsy showed a membranoproliferative pattern with IgM/C3 deposits and organized fibrillar cryoglobulin deposits; skin biopsy showed leukocytoclastic vasculitis.

Further workup found B-cell lymphoproliferative disease; entecavir was started when HBV DNA became positive before immunosuppression, and methylprednisolone, prednisolone, and rituximab improved proteinuria and renal function.

BUN has a source discrepancy: the narrative lists 35.8 mg/dL and Table 1 lists 24.6 mg/dL; the table value was structured.
